newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Star Telecom in one-for-five rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Star Telecom in one-for-five rights plan.

text.p: Star Telecom International Holdings Ltd said on Monday it planned to raise HK$185 million after expenses through a one-for-five rights issue.
The company said in a statement it would issue 104.99 million new shares at HK$1.80 per share, which represents a 14.3 percent discount to Star Telecom's closing price of HK$2.10 on Friday.

Star Telecom said the proceeds would be used to reduce bank borrowings and develop existing projects, which include a joint venture with the Chinese military to build mobile phone networks in 20 mainland provinces.
Glory Eagle, a wholly-owned subsidiary of China Strategic Holdings, has agreed to underwrite all the new issue, charging a fee of two percent of the proceeds.
If Glory Eagle is required to take up all the new shares pursuant to the underwriting agreement, China Strategic will control 16.7 percent of Star Telecom's enlarged share capital, it said.

Star Telecom chairman Wong Kam-fu and his wife Chu Wai-fun together hold 55.1 percent of the company's existing shares. They said they had no intention of taking up the new shares which would be allotted to them, the company said.
Their interest in Star Telecom would be diluted to 45.9 percent, it said.
